title: My week so far
grammar: Present perfect: ever, never, just, already, yet

scene.speaker: nova
scene.bubble: Read Mateo's diary of a busy week, learn the present perfect, then tell us what you have done.
scene.intro: The Inspiring Nordic year has just started, and it is already full of things to do. In this unit you read Mateo's diary of the first week, you learn the present perfect — the tense we use to say what we have and haven't done — and you talk about your own week. Have you ever kept a diary? By the end of this lesson you will be able to say what you have already done and what you haven't finished yet. Let's begin.

data.author: mateo
data.title: Our first week!
data.text:
What a week! The Inspiring Nordic year has just started, and we are already very busy.

On Monday, our teacher put us in project groups. My group has already chosen its topic: local jobs in our town. I have never worked in a group like this before, and I love it.

Sofía has finished the first chapters of Charlotte's Web — she reads every night! Liam hasn't started the reading yet, because he has football practice every day. Nadia has just made the first drawing for our poster, and it looks amazing.

I have done a lot this week too. I have tidied our project table, written my first notes and helped Liam with his homework. But I haven't chosen my job for the poster yet.

Have you had a busy week? What have you already done, and what haven't you finished yet? Write and tell us!

data.title: Present perfect
data.intro: We use the present perfect for experiences and for recent actions when the exact time is not important. We form it with have / has + the past participle.
rules: Form: have / has + past participle (finished, read, done, made…).
Use already and just in positive sentences; use yet in negatives and questions.
Use ever in questions and never in negatives to talk about experiences.

activities.title: Speaking — talk about your week. In pairs, then record it.

data.text: Ask and answer with a partner, using the present perfect. Model: “What have you already done today?” — “I have already had breakfast and tidied my room.”  1) What have you already done today? 2) Have you ever read Charlotte's Web? 3) What haven't you finished yet this week? 4) Have you ever won a game? Tell your partner about it. 5) What have you just learned in this unit? Then record your best answers.

homework.prompt: Write a short diary entry (5–6 sentences) about your week for the Inspiring Nordic blog, using the present perfect: something you have already done, something you haven't done yet, something you have just finished, a place you have never been, and something you have done this week that made you happy. Capital letters and full stops!

outcomes.puede: Catch the key points in the class news and write the missing word in each gap (A2 Key Listening).
Talk about experiences and this week's activities using the present perfect (A2 Key Speaking).
Read a diary and understand what a person has and hasn't done this week (A2 Key Reading).
Write a short diary using the present perfect, with correct capital letters and full stops.
Present perfect (have/has + past participle) with ever, never, just, already and yet; routine words.
